stages.name: Runner start
stages.summary: Loads the data package once and builds the LLM closure `complete`, then hands out one fresh ProcuDealAgent per case.
details: DataPackage(data) and package.lookup('') build the ID index once, shared by all cases (cli.py:41-42).
complete = llm_from_env() runs for every non-naive agent, procudeal included (cli.py:43). It only builds a client; no model call here.
llm_from_env reads os.environ['LLM_MODEL'] with no default (llm.py:56): if it is missing, the runner stops with a KeyError although the engine never calls the model.
Each ProcuDealAgent builds an LLMAgent(complete, package) as its fallback (procudeal/__init__.py:27).

stages.name: Open session, read quotes
stages.summary: Opens the case on the arena; every supplier's quote e-mail arrives at once (round 0). Every attachment is downloaded and turned into text.
details: From here the 60 s clock runs per thread (brief/api.md:75).
fetch_documents adds att['text'] to each attachment (play.py:118-123); the quote PDF text is what standard_terms() parses.
A 409 'one session per case in the final' resumes the running session instead (play.py:46-49).

stages.name: Move loop, cap check, dispatch
stages.summary: While any thread is live, the runner asks ProcuDealAgent.decide for one decision; it creates the Negotiator on a case's first move and runs the engine inside try/except. Near a Live Final wave cap the runner uses closing_move instead.
details: Cap check: time.time() > cap - max(CLOSE_BEFORE_CAP_S=90, slowest round + ROUND_MARGIN_S=15) (play.py:155).
No deadline in `arena play`, `arena run --set practice` or bench.py: closing_move never fires there.
A decision slower than 45 s (0.75 x MOVE_LIMIT_S) only logs a warning (play.py:160-161).
One decision per loop pass: the loop is single-threaded per case, so in RFQ cases threads are served one at a time.
ProcuDealAgent.decide (procudeal/__init__.py:31): new Negotiator when case_id changes; remember_prices() runs but its result is never read.
Engine move with 'action' -> {'action': ...}; otherwise writer.offer_email builds the e-mail (__init__.py:38-45).
Any engine exception -> kit LLMAgent.decide, trace source 'kit-llm' (__init__.py:47-49).

stages.name: Setup: C_open, limit, ceilings
stages.summary: Prices every opening quote with the supplier's standard terms, takes the cheapest that keeps the must-haves as C_open, and sets the walk-away limit to min(C_alt, C_open).
details: First pass without supplier estimates (policy.py:85-86), then again with each side's estimate (policy.py:90-99).
C_open stays infinite when no opening quote keeps the must-haves; the limit is then min(C_alt, inf).
ceiling = price_ceiling(mix, limit): the highest unit price on our term mix with C < limit; None becomes 0.0 (policy.py:100-102).
Runs inside the first move's 60 s window (observed ~0.02 s in runs/P18).

stages.name: Dossier and claim bank
stages.summary: Reads the supplier's owner type, documents and news from SQLite to estimate its cost of money and full cost, then builds every data claim the package supports, strongest first.
details: interest_rate = OWNER_RATE[owner_type] (group 0.05, private 0.07, family 0.075, founder 0.10; default 0.075), +0.05 if CASH_SIGNS match.
full_cost: own-plant should_cost row, else generic row x COUNTRY_COST, else quote price x (1 - 0.10).
wants_work and capacity_full are computed but never used by the policy.
Claim bank: notice period, index falls, should-cost, scorecard, forecast; each claim kept only if every ref exists in the package or case facts (claims.py:42).
A failing claim builder is logged and skipped (claims.py:38-39).

stages.name: Term mix, anchor, health price
stages.summary: Searches every allowed mix of non-price terms for the one that costs us least at equal value to the supplier, converts its quote to that mix, and sets the first offer (anchor) a fixed share below it.
details: plan_terms tries up to MAX_COMBOS=2000 term_options combinations (economics.py:106-138).
anchor = quote-on-our-mix x (ANCHOR[goal] + shift); ANCHOR leverage 0.80, routine 0.84, quality_first 0.88, secure_supply 0.90, stabilise 0.92, else 0.85.
shift -0.03 if reply delay >= 4 days or owner founder; +0.03 if owner group and delay <= 2 days.
stabilise / secure_supply: anchor = max(anchor, best_for_us) where best_for_us minimises C incl. the relationship charge.
price_increase cases: anchor = min(anchor, current_unit_price).

stages.name: Read the supplier's reply
stages.summary: For each new supplier e-mail: regex-read asks and traits, cap the full-cost estimate by its price, convert its standing price to our term mix, and react (re-plan on a payment ask, drop index claims if hedged, adopt a cheaper alternative sheet it sent).
details: Asks accumulate over the thread; traits are from the latest e-mail only.
bound_full_cost: full_cost <= max(price x 0.995, error-band floor) (dossier.py:67-73).
payment ask (once, if payment_days negotiable): interest_rate += 0.05 unless cash_need already set it, then replan (policy.py:306-310).
A supplier alternative sheet that keeps must-haves and costs us > EUR 1 less than its standing sheet becomes our mix (policy.py:313-331).
side.ceiling is not recomputed when the mix changes.

stages.name: Accept check, board, readiness
stages.summary: Prices every live supplier's standing sheet. A sheet can be accepted only with a price, all must-haves kept, and C below min(C_alt, C_open). Each thread is then marked ready or not.
details: accept_check: C >= limit -> 'C x does not beat the limit y' (economics.py:53-55).
ready: final_offer, or moves_left <= 1, or agreed (unless below the health band), or its price within 0.5 % of our last offer, or (relationship goals) at best_for_us.
board: every live standing sheet with a price that keeps the must-haves (the limit is not applied); leader = lowest C.

stages.name: RFQ: drop rule and reverse auction
stages.when: every move, RFQ only (more than 1 live thread)
stages.summary: Once the leader is ready, the cheapest runner-up gets one 'last call' to beat the leader's C by 2 %. While each call improves the best C by at least 0.5 %, the new runner-up is called; then the best sheet is accepted. Bidders more than 10 % above the leader stop getting rounds.
details: AUCTION_EDGE 0.02, AUCTION_MIN_GAIN 0.005, AUCTION_CALLS 4, DROP_GAP 0.10.
A bidder at final_offer is never called; an agreed bidder can be.
Drop rule needs at least 2 prices from the bidder (its quote + one reply).

stages.name: Close or walk
stages.summary: Accept the best passing sheet when its supplier is ready (or every thread is). Walk away when nothing passes and every thread is at final_offer or out of messages.
details: Trace why for an accept: '<ready reason>; C x below the limit y' (policy.py:560-562).
walk_away goes to live[0]; it ends the whole case.

stages.name: Next price, term sheets, claims
stages.summary: Picks the thread that waited longest, computes the next price by closing a share of the gap, and builds up to 3 term sheets that cost us the same, plus claim and answer sentences.
details: Gap share: 0.30 per round, 0.10 after a deep (>= 6 %) drop, 0.45 when the supplier says it is stuck, 0 (its price) when its price is frozen.
Price is capped at the ceiling and at 0.998 x its price on our mix; never below our last price except by those caps.
Claims: 3 in the first e-mail, 2 after a data request, else 1; in RFQ the rival's offer is cited first.

stages.name: E-mail writer (template)
stages.summary: Wraps the move in a fixed English e-mail: greeting, answers, claim sentences, a line about the packages, sign-off. No model is called.
details: Subject: 'Re: ' + the supplier's last subject (or case title), max 300 chars.
refs = sorted set of every claim's data IDs.

stages.name: Send, read reply, record trace
stages.summary: Posts the message; the call blocks until the supplier replies (up to about a minute). An action ends the loop. A 409 (late, ended, round limit) is turned into a reply or a result.
outputs: supplier reply appended to the thread
details: accept / walk_away -> table.close -> return result (play.py:164-166).
409 -> table.missed: case ended -> result; thread closed -> status walked_away; else the timeout answer (play.py:74-90).
409 on an action while the case runs -> append the reply and decide again (play.py:173-175).
Any other ArenaError is re-raised and stops this case (play.py:169-170).
Trace entry written before sending (__init__.py:50); bench.py saves agent.trace as 'decisions' (bench.py:67).

stages.name: Fallbacks: kit LLM, naive, closing move
stages.summary: Only when the engine raises: one LLM call writes the move, guarded by code; if the LLM fails, the naive agent moves. Separately, near a Live Final wave cap the runner closes with closing_move (no LLM).
details: LLM call timeout 45 s (both providers); Anthropic SDK default max_retries 2 applies.
NaiveAgent accepts without a must-have or alternative check.
closing_move: cheapest live standing sheet that keeps must-haves and has C < C_alt, else walk_away (play.py:126-139).

pricing.summary: All numbers come from the kit's total_cost. The engine picks the non-price term mix that is cheapest for us at equal value to the supplier, converts each supplier price to that mix, opens at a fixed share below it, then closes 30 % of the gap per round, capped where C would reach min(C_alt, C_open). Extra sheets are priced to cost us exactly the same as the main sheet.

steps.name: Opening cost and limit
steps.formula: c_open = min(total_cost(case, t, std, est) for opening quotes with a price and must_haves_ok); limit = min(alternative_cost(case), c_open)
steps.explain: A deal must cost less than the cheapest opening quote and the no-deal alternative. If no opening keeps the must-haves, c_open stays infinite.

steps.name: Supplier estimate
steps.formula: {'standard': reference terms, 'interest_rate': OWNER_RATE[owner] (+0.05 cash), 'full_cost': should-cost | generic x COUNTRY_COST | quote x 0.90}
steps.explain: Used to value terms for the supplier and, in stabilise/secure_supply cases, to price the relationship charge.

steps.name: Term mix search
steps.formula: for mix in term_mixes (<= 2000): price = price_for_value(mix, supplier, value(quote)); C at price x deal_ratio; sort by (round(C), number of changed terms)
steps.explain: deal_ratio = (1 + anchor_ratio) / 2: mixes are compared at the price level we expect to close at. plan[0] becomes side.mix.

steps.name: Its price on our mix
steps.formula: _their_price = price_for_value(case, mix, est, supplier_value(case, standing_terms, est))
steps.explain: Every standing offer is restated as the price that would be worth the same to the supplier on our mix, so rounds compare like with like (side.theirs).

steps.name: Anchor
steps.formula: anchor = q_eq * (ANCHOR[goal] + shift); anchor = max(anchor, best_for_us); price_increase: anchor = min(anchor, current_unit_price)
steps.explain: leverage 0.80, routine 0.84, quality_first 0.88, secure_supply 0.90, stabilise 0.92 (else 0.85); shift +/-0.03 by owner type and reply delay.

steps.name: Health price (relationship goals)
steps.formula: best_for_us = cheapest_price(case, mix, std, est)  # golden-section search on C over [0.01, 3 x price scale]
steps.explain: Only for stabilise / secure_supply: below this price the relationship charge makes C rise again. Other goals: 0.

steps.name: Ceiling
steps.formula: ceiling = price_ceiling(case, mix, limit, std, est)  # bisection: highest price with C < limit, floored to cents; None -> 0.0
steps.explain: Set in setup for the setup mix. Not recomputed when the mix changes later. 0.0 is treated as 'no cap' by `if side.ceiling`.

steps.name: First offer
steps.explain: At least 1 % below its quote on our mix.

steps.name: Price frozen
steps.explain: Its e-mail says prices are frozen: match its price (then capped at 0.998 x) and win on terms. The next reply is then within 0.5 % and gets accepted.

steps.name: Stuck
steps.formula: price = max(ours[-1] + STUCK_STEP * (theirs - ours[-1]), ours[-1])  # STUCK_STEP 0.45
steps.explain: It says it cannot move without a move from us: bigger step.

steps.name: Normal concession
steps.formula: step = HOLD_STEP (0.10) if deep else STEP (0.30); price = max(ours[-1] + step * (theirs - ours[-1]), ours[-1])
steps.explain: deep = second offer after a first counter that dropped >= 6 %, or (RFQ) its last drop >= 6 %.

steps.name: Health override
steps.formula: if relationship goal and best_for_us and ours and theirs < best_for_us * 0.98: price = min(best_for_us, ceiling or inf)
steps.explain: Evaluated first in next_price: never push a strategic supplier below a healthy margin.

steps.name: Caps
steps.formula: if side.ceiling: price = min(price, side.ceiling); price = min(price, theirs * 0.998); round(max(price, 0.01), 2)
steps.explain: We never offer at or above its own price; the 0.998 cap plus CLOSE_GAP 0.005 means a supplier that stands still is accepted next round.

steps.name: Main sheet
steps.formula: main = complete_offer(case, {**side.mix, 'unit_price': price}); c_main = total_cost(case, main, std)
steps.explain: c_main has no relationship estimate: iso-cost sheets use our cash cost only.

steps.name: Extra sheets (max 3)
steps.formula: first e-mail: up to 2 plan[1:] mixes at equal_cost_price(mix, c_main); later: its own mix at equal cost; RFQ non-leader: the leader's mix at equal cost (inserted at 1); clause ask: best-deadband index clause at equal cost (inserted at 1 if room)
steps.explain: Sheets that cost us the same let the supplier's choice show what it values. Relationship goals drop extra sheets priced below best_for_us x 0.995.

steps.name: Accept check
steps.formula: ok = price present and must_haves_ok and total_cost(terms, std, est) < min(C_alt, c_open)
steps.explain: The only gate before any engine accept; the sheet ID is always the supplier's current standing sheet.

rfq.summary: With more than one live thread the engine runs the threads round-robin (oldest reply first), cites the best rival bid, offers the leader's term package to the others, stops talking to bidders more than 10 % above the leader in C, and once the leader is ready runs a short reverse auction (up to 4 last calls) before accepting the best sheet in C. Accepting one sheet ends the case.

steps.name: RFQ mode
steps.action: self.rfq = True; if bidders walk away and one is left, the single-thread rules apply

steps.name: Round-robin
steps.condition: several threads can be talked to
steps.action: pick the lowest side.seen = total prices seen across all threads when its last reply arrived (oldest reply first)

steps.name: Leader board
steps.condition: standing sheet with a price that keeps the must-haves
steps.action: board[sid] = (C with estimate, sheet_id, terms); leader = lowest C

steps.name: Rival claim
steps.condition: talking to a non-leader: cite the leader; talking to the leader: cite the bidder with the lowest unit price below its own; each rival sheet once per thread
steps.action: first claim: 'Another supplier has offered EUR x per unit for this part (offer:...)'

steps.name: Leader's package
steps.condition: non-leader thread, fewer than 3 sheets, leader's mix differs
steps.action: add a sheet on the leader's term mix at the same C to us (position 1)

steps.name: Leader terms line
steps.condition: a rival claim was used and the leader has a shorter lead time and/or longer payment terms
steps.action: 'That offer also comes with ...' (words only, no figures)

steps.name: Small steps after a big drop
steps.action: concede 10 % of the gap instead of 30 %

steps.name: Drop rule
steps.condition: non-leader with >= 2 prices and C > leader C x 1.10
steps.action: dropped: no more rounds (unless no other thread can be talked to)

steps.name: Auction start
steps.condition: best passing sheet is the leader's and the leader is ready (agreed, final_offer, within 0.5 %, last move, health price)
steps.action: call the runner-up with the lowest C (not dropped, not final_offer, moves left)

steps.name: Last call
steps.condition: equal_cost_price(runner mix, leader C x 0.98) exists and keeps must-haves
steps.action: one sheet at that price (max 0.998 x its price) + rival claim + fixed text: 'Another supplier has agreed to terms that cost us less overall...'

steps.name: Judge the call
steps.condition: after the runner's reply: best C improved by < 0.5 %, or 4 calls made
steps.action: accept the best sheet ('best after N auction call(s)')

steps.name: Next call
steps.condition: best C improved by >= 0.5 % (the runner overtook the leader)
steps.action: call the new runner-up (often the old leader), without waiting for it to be ready

steps.name: No runner left
steps.condition: no runner can be called and >= 1 call was made
steps.action: accept best ('..., no runner-up left'); if no call was made, the normal accept_ready rule accepts the ready leader

examples: Two bidders (sandbox D02, practice run at commit f358cfe-dirty): the engine alternates counters J1, C1, J1, C1 for 5 rounds. J1 answers with final_offer and is the leader in C, so it is ready. C1 gets one last call to beat J1's C by 2 %. Its reply does not improve the best C by 0.5 %, so the engine accepts J1: 'best after 1 auction call(s); C 186,560 below the limit 214,296'.

Three bidders (practice P05, commit f358cfe-dirty): all three get a first offer. After its first reply, sup:70240 is more than 10 % above the leader in C and is dropped (it got 1 message in total). sup:70250 reaches agreed and leads; sup:70210 gets a last call, beats it by at least 0.5 % and becomes the leader; sup:70250 (agreed, not final) gets the next call; that does not improve the best C enough, so sup:70210 is accepted after 2 calls.
Leader at final_offer, runner also at final_offer: no runner can be called (final_offer is never pushed) and no call was made, so rfq_close returns None and accept_ready takes the leader at once.

Nothing passes: if every live bidder is at final_offer or out of messages and no standing sheet beats min(C_alt, C_open), the engine walks away from the whole case ('no standing sheet passes the accept check').

stop_reasons.effect: accept; why 'final_offer; C x below the limit y'. In saved practice runs this is the most common end (P02, P04, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18), after 2-5 rounds

stop_reasons.effect: accept if the sheet passes; why starts with the status text ('open; ...'). The 10th message is never a counter

stop_reasons.trigger: supplier status agreed (it offers exactly one of our sheets), not below the health band
stop_reasons.effect: accept; why 'agreed; ...'

stop_reasons.trigger: its price on our mix <= our last price x 1.005
stop_reasons.effect: accept; why 'within half a percent of our offer; ...'

stop_reasons.trigger: stabilise/secure_supply: its price on our mix <= best_for_us and >= best_for_us x 0.98
stop_reasons.effect: accept; why 'at the price that is cheapest for us with the relationship charge; ...'

stop_reasons.trigger: every live thread is ready and the best sheet passes
stop_reasons.effect: accept the best sheet in C

stop_reasons.trigger: RFQ: after a last call the best C improved by < 0.5 %, or 4 calls made
stop_reasons.effect: accept; why 'best after N auction call(s); ...'

stop_reasons.trigger: RFQ: at least one call made and no runner-up can be called
stop_reasons.effect: accept; why 'best after N auction call(s), no runner-up left; ...'

stop_reasons.trigger: no live thread has moves_left > 0 and a sheet passes
stop_reasons.effect: accept; why 'no moves left; ...'

stop_reasons.trigger: no standing sheet passes the accept check and every live thread is final_offer or out of messages
stop_reasons.effect: walk_away: case ends without a deal (scores the alternative)

stop_reasons.trigger: no thread has moves left and nothing passes
stop_reasons.effect: walk_away

stop_reasons.trigger: engine exception; the LLM answers accept or walk_away and the guard passes it
stop_reasons.effect: accept (must-haves kept, C <= C_alt) or walk_away (no check)

stop_reasons.trigger: engine exception and the LLM fails or its reply fails the guard
stop_reasons.effect: naive: accept at agreed / final_offer / no moves / within 1 % (no must-have or alternative check); walk_away if no supplier quotes a price

stop_reasons.trigger: Live Final only: now > wave cap - max(90 s, slowest round + 15 s)
stop_reasons.effect: accept the cheapest live sheet with must-haves kept and C < C_alt (no C_open check, no relationship charge), else walk_away

stop_reasons.trigger: every thread is walked_away / no_bid
stop_reasons.effect: play() returns table.result()

stop_reasons.trigger: an ArenaError other than 409 (e.g. 422 on a stale term_sheet_id, 5xx after retries) or any exception outside the agent
stop_reasons.effect: play() raises; the case stops being played. In the final the session stays open until the wave cap (no deal)

stop_reasons.trigger: supplier ends its thread (status walked_away)
stop_reasons.effect: thread no longer live; if it was the last live thread the reply carries the result and play() returns it

stop_reasons.trigger: supplier declines to quote (status no_bid)
stop_reasons.effect: thread not live from the start

stop_reasons.trigger: our messages in a thread reach case.round_limit (default 10)
stop_reasons.effect: a further send gets 409; accept is still allowed. The engine stops countering at moves_left <= 1 anyway

stop_reasons.trigger: a message later than 60 s after the supplier's last reply; 3 in a row, or one after the last round
stop_reasons.effect: 409; our last offer is repeated and patience drops; after 3 the thread ends (missed() marks it walked_away)

stop_reasons.trigger: Live Final wave cap (8 min, read seconds_left)
stop_reasons.effect: every open session ends without a deal (end_reason wave_cap); later calls 409 -> missed() returns the result

stop_reasons.trigger: session end_reason no_deal, timeout or window_closed (brief/api.md:122)
stop_reasons.effect: case ends; the runner sees it as a result or a 409

constants.name: ANCHOR
constants.meaning: First offer as a share of its quote on our mix, by category goal (default 0.85 for other goals, policy.py:118).

constants.name: STEP
constants.meaning: Share of the gap we close per round.

constants.name: HOLD_STEP
constants.meaning: Gap share after a deep drop (2nd offer, or RFQ last drop).

constants.name: DEEP_DROP
constants.meaning: A price drop this large counts as deep.

constants.name: CLOSE_GAP
constants.meaning: Ready when its price is within this of our last offer.

constants.name: FIRST_CLAIMS
constants.meaning: Claims in the first e-mail to a supplier.

constants.name: LATER_CLAIMS
constants.meaning: Claims per later e-mail.

constants.name: DATA_CLAIMS
constants.meaning: Claims after it asked for data.

constants.name: DROP_GAP
constants.meaning: RFQ: a bidder this far above the leader's C gets no more rounds.

constants.name: AUCTION_EDGE
constants.meaning: RFQ last call asks the runner-up to beat the leader's C by this.

constants.name: AUCTION_MIN_GAIN
constants.meaning: Keep calling while the best C improves at least this much.

constants.name: AUCTION_CALLS
constants.meaning: At most this many last calls.

llm.engine_note: policy.py, economics.py, claims.py, dossier.py, signals.py and writer.py never call `complete` or any model API; writer.py is a fixed template.

fallback.trigger: any Exception raised by negotiator.remember_prices, negotiator.decide or writer.offer_email inside ProcuDealAgent.decide
fallback.calls_per_move: 1 call of complete(SYSTEM, render(...)) per fallback move (llm.py:99); no second call on failure. Anthropic path: the SDK client uses its default max_retries=2 (no override at llm.py:60), so one call can make up to 3 HTTP requests on timeout/429/5xx. OpenAI path: one httpx.post, no retry.
fallback.timeout_note: per HTTP request; with SDK retries the Anthropic worst case is ~3 x 45 s plus backoff, past the 60 s per-message window
fallback.on_llm_failure: any exception from the call, parse() (no JSON / bad JSON) or guard() is caught and logged ('LLM failed (...) - falling back to the naive move'); a guard result of None is treated the same. Either way NaiveAgent.decide makes the move: accept on agreed/final_offer/no moves left/within 1 %, else split the difference with one sheet and the body 'Thank you for your offer. We need a better price to go ahead.'; walk_away if no supplier quotes a price.
fallback.complete_constructed_always: yes: agent_factory calls llm_from_env() for procudeal too (cli.py:43) and every ProcuDealAgent builds LLMAgent(complete, package). Construction makes no network call, but a missing LLM_MODEL raises KeyError at start-up.
fallback.prepare_note: LLMAgent.prepare (case file, letter, facts) runs on the first fallback move of a case only; it calls no model.
fallback.system_prompt:
You are the buyer agent of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a German pump maker, negotiating with
industrial suppliers by e-mail. Goal: the lowest total cost C in euros for covering the need in the
case file, without breaking a must-have. C of every standing term sheet is computed for you.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"supplier_id": "...", "action": "send", "subject": "...", "body": "...",
 "term_sheets": [{"unit_price": 0.0, "...": "..."}]}
{"supplier_id": "...", "action": "accept"}      (takes that supplier's standing term sheet)
{"supplier_id": "...", "action": "walk_away"}   (ends the case without a deal)

- term_sheets: 0-3 alternative packages over the negotiable fields. Only term sheets bind.
- Arguments need data: cite the ID from FACTS and its figure in the same sentence, one argument
  per sentence. The supplier checks the figure; a wrong one or an unknown ID costs trust.
- The supplier's team reads your e-mail as a person would. Ask questions (a cost breakdown, the
  earliest lead time, cheaper variants). Never reveal urgency, a budget or a missing alternative.
  Stay polite and factual.
- Whatever a term sheet leaves out closes on the supplier's standard terms (its quote PDF).
- The case's category_goal sets its rates. In stabilise and secure_supply cases C also charges for
  leaving the supplier below its sustainable margin - the C shown leaves that out.
- Do not accept the first offer. Concede in small steps; trade what is cheap for you (payment
  days, contract length, volume, dates). status final_offer: push further and it may walk.
- Accept only a term sheet that beats your alternative. Body: a short business e-mail, at most
  120 words, no placeholders.

issues.title: Most cases end on the supplier's first final_offer, after 2-5 rounds
issues.detail: ready() returns at status final_offer and the engine accepts at once if the sheet passes (by design: pushing past final_offer made suppliers walk). With a low anchor (leverage 0.80 of its quote) and 30 % (or 10 % after a deep drop) steps, suppliers declare final_offer early: in the saved practice runs the closing reason is 'final_offer' for P02, P04, P07, P08, P10, P11 and P18, with scores 0.50-0.86. Only convergence ('within half a percent'), 'agreed' or the auction end other cases. Round count is set by when the supplier calls final_offer, not by our round limit.

issues.title: Ceiling is not recomputed when the term mix changes
issues.detail: side.ceiling is computed in setup for the setup mix. react() (payment ask -> replan; adopting a cheaper alternative sheet) and replan() replace side.mix, but next_price keeps capping with the old ceiling. On a mix that is dearer for us (e.g. faster payment) the old ceiling is too high: we can offer a sheet whose C fails the limit, and an 'agreed' answer then cannot be accepted. On a cheaper mix it caps concessions too early.

issues.title: Ceiling 0.0 means 'no price passes' but is read as 'no cap'
issues.detail: price_ceiling returns None when no price on the mix beats the limit; setup stores 0.0 and next_price uses `if side.ceiling:` and `side.ceiling or math.inf`, so the price is not capped at all. The accept check still blocks a bad accept, but the engine negotiates rounds that cannot end in an acceptable deal, then walks.

issues.title: C_open becomes infinite when the opening quote breaks a must-have
issues.detail: setup() only counts openings that keep the must-haves. If none does, c_open = inf, limit = min(C_alt, inf) and ceiling = inf: no price cap and any must-have-keeping sheet below C_alt passes. The arena still scores against the opening's C: in runs/P10 the engine logged 'below the limit inf' while the arena's c_open was 1,932,492. A deal above the arena's C_open would score 0.

issues.title: Naive fallback accepts without any check
issues.detail: If the engine raises and the LLM call fails (timeout, bad JSON) or its reply fails the guard, NaiveAgent.decide moves. It accepts at agreed, final_offer, no moves left or within 1 % with no must-have and no alternative check. A broken must-have scores 0.

issues.title: LLM fallback can miss the 60 s window
issues.detail: anthropic.Anthropic(timeout=45.0) keeps the SDK default max_retries=2, which retries timeouts, 429 and 5xx. One fallback move can take ~3 x 45 s plus backoff; max_tokens is 16000. A late message counts as a timeout. CLAUDE.md asks for <= 30 s. Only on the exception path.

issues.title: procudeal needs LLM_MODEL set although the engine never calls a model
issues.detail: agent_factory always calls llm_from_env(), which reads os.environ['LLM_MODEL'] with no default. Without it the runner stops with KeyError before the first case, including the Live Final runner.

issues.title: A partial setup failure sends every later move to the LLM
issues.detail: setup() fills self.sides one supplier at a time. If new_side raises for the 2nd supplier, self.sides is non-empty, so setup never reruns and observe(self.sides[sid]) raises KeyError on every move: the whole case runs on the kit LLM fallback.

issues.title: RFQ rival claim can cite a higher price
issues.detail: For a non-leader the cited rival is the leader in C, whatever its unit price. If the leader wins on terms but quotes a higher unit price, the e-mail says 'Another supplier has offered EUR x' with x above the addressee's own price, which reveals a weaker number. leader_terms_line adds words only for lead time and payment days.

issues.title: RFQ threads are served one at a time while every thread's clock runs
issues.detail: play() is single-threaded per case and each send blocks until that supplier replies (up to about a minute). The 60 s clock runs per thread from the supplier's reply (api.md:75), and the engine has no per-thread elapsed time. With 2-3 bidders and slow replies, the leader can wait through several auction calls before the accept arrives. No timeouts are seen in the saved practice runs (fast replies), but final latency is unknown.

issues.title: Third talk list can counter a supplier at final_offer
issues.detail: If no thread that is not ready has moves left and nothing passes yet (e.g. RFQ: A at final_offer above the limit, B open on its last message), `talk = [s for s in live if moves_left > 0]` includes ready threads, so the engine may send a counter to a final_offer supplier, which the team found makes suppliers walk.

issues.title: Last-move accept wastes the 10th message and mislabels the reason
issues.detail: ready() fires at moves_left <= 1, so at most 9 counters are sent per thread (the arena allows accept after the round limit). The reason is `status or "last move"`, which is 'open' for an open thread, so the trace reads 'open; C ...'.

issues.title: Last-call text says the rival 'agreed' even when it did not
issues.detail: The fixed text 'Another supplier has agreed to terms that cost us less overall' is sent whenever the leader is ready, which also covers final_offer, within 0.5 %, last move and the health price; after the first call the leader may be the previous runner-up that never agreed.

issues.title: Auction only tries the cheapest runner-up
issues.detail: If last_call_offer returns None for the cheapest runner (no equal-cost price, or a must-have broken), no other runner is tried; with no earlier call the leader is accepted at once.

issues.title: C_open and later C use different supplier estimates
issues.detail: c_open is fixed in setup with the setup estimate; later accept checks use the current estimate, which changes (bound_full_cost lowers full_cost each reply; a payment ask raises interest_rate). Only stabilise / secure_supply cases are affected (relationship charge).

issues.title: Equal-cost sheets ignore the relationship charge
issues.detail: c_main = total_cost(case, main, std) without the estimate, so in strategic cases the 'equal cost' alternatives are not equal for us once the health charge counts; the 0.995 x best_for_us floor filter only removes the cheapest ones.

issues.title: No-price quote gives a EUR 0.01 first offer
issues.detail: If its quote has no unit_price, anchor = 0 x ratio = 0 and side.theirs starts at inf, so next_price returns max(0, 0.01) = 0.01.

issues.title: Dead code and unused signals
issues.detail: DONE (policy.py:38) is never used; remember_prices runs every move but _sheet_price is never called; Dossier.wants_work, capacity_full and notes are computed but never read, so 'looks for work' or 'capacity full' have no effect on the offer.

issues.title: Run files contain Infinity
issues.detail: bench.py writes json.dumps(..., default=str) with allow_nan on, so an infinite ceiling is saved as Infinity (all runs/P10 files). JavaScript JSON.parse rejects it; the web loader must sanitise.

issues.title: closing_move ignores C_open and the relationship charge
issues.detail: At the wave cap the runner accepts any must-have-keeping sheet with C < C_alt, priced without the supplier estimate. A deal above C_open scores 0, and in strategic cases a squeeze deal can cost more than it shows. Only in the Live Final.
